newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Easter holidays to dampen trade in SAfrican shares.
newsitem.headline: Easter holidays to dampen trade in SAfrican shares.

text.p: The four-day week next week in South Africa will quieten trade and reduce volumes traded on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, dealers and portfolio managers said on Thursday.
Next week sees the four-day long Easter weekend and, coupled with school holidays, most dealers were seen taking leave.
"The Easter long weekend will quieten the market. There will be activity before the (U.S. Federal Reserve) meeting but it will taper down on the 26th and 27th," a dealer said.
Industrials were seen continuing the recovery started this year.

"We see continued firming in industrials driven by the IT sector, construction, insurance, property, beverages hotels and leisure, and the recovery in the stores sector continuing," Grahame Graham-Parker, general manager at Infinity Asset management, told Reuters.
He said the index would move towards the 8,700 level set last in January in the next couple of weeks.
Dealers and portfolio managers said the March quarter reporting season for unit trusts would also boost sentiment.
"(The close-out) would bode well for continued strength in the industrial sector," Graham-Parker said.
Concerns of a rate hike in the U.S. will keep interest in the market as players await direction from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan on Tuesday on a possible interest rate hike.
But dealers said a rate hike had already largely been discounted in the market.
Gold shares are set to continue weak next week despite the recovery in the gold price.
"Gold shares have seen another correction in a bear market in gold...the general trend is to remain down weak-on-weak," Graham Parker said.
There are no major company results expected next week and the market will look for local guidance from February trade data and CPI figures.
CPI is expected to rise to 9.75 percent from 9.4 percent in January year-on-year. The month-on-month rate of increase is expected to slow to 0.45 percent after 1.3 percent in January.
The trade forecast at a 1.04 billion rand surplus from a 0.52 billion surplus in January.
